title: Does Debate Survive When Both Debaters Share the Same Blind Spot?

original_idea.body:
# Does Debate Survive When Both Debaters Share the Same Blind Spot?

**Problem:** If both debaters come from the same model and share a factual blind spot, neither can surface the truth -- an untested single-model-debate failure.

**Direction:** Identify questions a given small open model reliably gets wrong. Run self-debate (same model, both sides) on these vs cross-model debate (a different model on one side). Measure how often each setup lets the weak judge reach the correct answer.

**Why it matters:** Many practical debate setups use one model for both sides; shared blind spots could give false assurance.

**Relevant context:** Kenton et al. (2024); Khan et al. (2024); arXiv:2510.11235.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Strong chain: shared-blind-spot self-debate giving false assurance is a defensible debate-failure result.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Correlated-failure debate-robustness probe, external-friendly, no internal access.

novelty.reasoning: Shared-error concern noted; the self-vs-cross-model blind-spot test may be open.
